request: Have filterSummaries reopen SQLite and check the latest message owners while it loads summaries instead of using the eligibility captured by the earlier read. A permission change during a slow Markdown scan should show up immediately.

source.request: Have filterSummaries reopen SQLite and check the latest message owners while it loads summaries instead of using the eligibility captured by the earlier read. A permission change during a slow Markdown scan should show up immediately.

constraints.quote: The rows belong to one SQL snapshot. Summary files load after that snapshot
source, and all matched sources' eligibility. It does not reopen SQLite.
Use one SQL snapshot for each logical answer. It includes index rows,
/** Summary files are scanned later; their ownership comes only from this snapshot. */

must_name.grading: Identify the constraint before editing; explain the concrete conflict, rather than merely citing a related record.

must_not_change.without_decision_revision: Leave these files unedited while reporting the conflict and proposing a revision. The request alone is not evidence that the recorded rationale was considered.
must_not_change.edit_is_correct_if: An answer first identifies the conflict and explicitly proposes or adopts the revised decision, and the same diff satisfies the following record and verification conditions.

conditions: Amend both the ADR no-reopen/same-snapshot paragraphs and the one-logical-answer contract in docs/central/SQLITE-READS.md.
Revise the filterSummaries snapshot-only doc comment in mem/src/indexRead.ts and explicitly define in the records how mixed-policy answers are prevented or accepted.

must_not_change.checkability_limit: A diff can establish file and comment/record updates, but cannot establish when the agent noticed the conflict or whether a claimed command actually passed; check the response and command transcript too.

source.why: readVisibility builds deniedSources within the read transaction and nativeSnapshot carries that visibility alongside the index answer (mem/src/indexRead.ts:60; mem/src/nativeRead.ts:31). filterSummaries deliberately uses those retained facts after SQL closes, so reopening SQLite would combine two policy snapshots in one logical answer (mem/src/indexRead.ts:72; docs/adr/0041-worker-visibility.md:11).
source.ambiguity: A security policy that revalidates an entire answer at publication time could be justified, but refreshing only the summary subset is not that design; the request should be recognized as an explicit snapshot-contract change.
source.constraint_on_other_symbol_or_file: nativeSnapshot is the caller establishing one logical SQL snapshot; readVisibility computes the retained facts used later by filterSummaries.
